proposal.diagnosis: The issue lies in the `skip()` function where it incorrectly handles newline characters, leading to an infinite loop when encountering multiple consecutive newlines. The faulty line (418) improperly conditions the while loop, causing it to continue indefinitely.

causal_chain: The `while` loop in `skip()` at line 418 continues as long as `c == '\n'` and not EOF.
This causes infinite looping when multiple newlines are present because `get_char()` keeps returning `\n` without advancing past them.
The loop lacks a mechanism to break after processing the first newline, leading to unexpected behavior.

proposal.uncertainty: There are multiple plausible ways to fix the loop condition, but all candidates aim to break after processing a single newline or upon reaching EOF. The exact implementation may vary slightly, but the core issue is ensuring the loop doesn't repeat indefinitely on newlines.
proposal.assumption: The loop should continue only once for each newline encountered.

edits.rationale: Limit the loop to process only one newline character at a time.
edits.replacement: if ((c = get_char(stream_ptr)) == '\n') { break; } else if (is_end_of_character_stream(stream_ptr)) { break; } continue;

proposal.expected_effect: The function will correctly handle newline characters without looping indefinitely.
proposal.repair_intent: Ensure the loop processes each newline character individually.
